public_rationale: The crisis happened, and former directors explicitly connect their experience to pressure from profit incentives. However, OpenAI's investigation summary attributes the dismissal to lost trust and rejects several safety and financial explanations. These are competing causal accounts, not independently established portions of a mixed result. The available evidence does not settle Marcus's stronger claim that this structure inevitably produced conflict between profit-seekers and safety stewards.
limitations: Both principal causal accounts come from parties involved in the dispute.
The investigation summary addresses the dismissal more directly than the wider instability.
The metaphor and inevitability language lack a precise test.

statement.excerpt: The whole nonprofit-hybrid model, introduced in 2019 (the company was originally pure non-profit) was always a ticking time bomb, because the people trying to make money were never going to have a perfect relationship with those in the nonprofit that were charged with keeping the world safe.
statement.document_title: Top 5 reasons why OpenAI was probably never really worth $86 billion

from_speaker: was always a ticking time bomb
those in the nonprofit that were charged with keeping the world safe
our_interpretation: The ordinary reading is that conflicting commercial and safety responsibilities made the hybrid structure inherently unstable.
The surrounding reference to the recent drama makes the November 2023 governance crisis the principal historical test of that explanation.
Conflict occurring under this structure does not by itself establish that profit-versus-safety incentives caused it or made it inevitable.
criteria.support_condition: Governance records and credible accounts establish that competing commercial and nonprofit safety responsibilities materially caused the governance crisis. Establishing inevitability would require more than one instance of conflict.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Credible causal evidence establishes that the relevant conflict arose independently of the alleged commercial-versus-safety mechanism. A temporary period of cooperation alone would not contradict the claim.
